title: ControlFusion: A Controllable Image Fusion Network with Language-Vision De

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states that 2,050 clear images were selected and that DDL-12 contains 48,000 training image pairs and 4,800 test image pairs, generated from 12 degradation types at 4 levels. This is arithmetically inconsistent: 48,000 + 4,800 = 52,800 pairs, which would require 52,800 / (12 × 4) = 1,100 original image pairs, not 2,050 images. If each of the 2,050 images were used as a source pair, the number of generated pairs would be 2,050 × 12 × 4 = 98,400.

The text states that ControlFusion 'uniquely includes pre-enhancement by several SOTA image restoration algorithms tailored to each degradation type' while 'competing fusion methods are evaluated on raw degraded inputs without pre-enhancement steps, introducing an imbalance that favors our results.' This is an uncontrolled comparison: the pre-enhancement should be applied equally to all methods or omitted from all methods for a fair evaluation.

The text says scene depth is 'estimated by DepthAnything-V2 [40]', but reference [40] in the bibliography is Restormer by Zamir et al. (CVPR 2022), which is not a depth-estimation model and does not describe Depth Anything V2. The correct Depth Anything V2 citation is absent.

The paper says object detection was performed 'using the retrained YOLOv8 [26]', but reference [26] is the original YOLO paper by Redmon et al. (CVPR 2016). YOLOv8 is not described or introduced by that reference; the appropriate YOLOv8/Ultralytics citation is missing.

The efficiency comparison is misleading and internally inconsistent. The table separates restoration methods and fusion methods, but the final 'Methods' column includes only SegMiF*, Text-IF, Text-DiFuse, and ControlFusion, omitting other compared fusion methods. The text claims that once the two-stage restoration overhead is factored in, 'the efficiency advantages of our unified model become evident,' but no combined restoration+fusion totals are shown for the marked two-stage pipelines, so the table does not support that claim.

A.7 states, 'As demonstrated in Fig. 7 and Tab. 6, both CLIP and SFVA yield substantial improvements in restoration and fusion performance.' However, Fig. 7 is the qualitative ablation figure and Table 6 contains ablations for losses, PMM, and the frequency branch; none of these demonstrated a CLIP/text-encoder ablation. The sentence should refer to Table 8 or to an actual CLIP-ablation result, neither of which is present.

The text claims, 'The t-SNE results further validate the importance of frequency priors,' but no t-SNE visualization, plot, or quantitative t-SNE analysis appears anywhere in the paper or appendix. This is an unsupported assertion of a result that is not shown.

RoadScene is cited as reference [36] in Section 3 ('selected 2,050 high-quality clear images from RoadScene [36]') but as reference [35] in Section 5.1 ('RoadScene [35]'). Reference [36] is U2Fusion and reference [35] is FusionDN, so the citation of the RoadScene dataset is inconsistent between sections.
